Any r-ball satisfies r<=(sum_{j=n-k+1}^n(S_j-1))/(k+sqrt(k)); the symmetric center (1+r)1 achieves all bounds and any active k enforces uniqueness. Positive integer A_k give rational ratios A_k/A_l on ties. If k != l and neither sqrt is rational, rearranging sqrt(k)=q sqrt(l)+q*l-k and conjugating irrational parts forces k=l; hence simultaneous ties require both square indices. Construct any T subset square indices via M=100n^4 and A_j=M(j+sqrt(j)) for j in T or M*j+floor(Msqrt(j))+1 otherwise. A nonsquare singleton is selected by bounded additive offsets 1 versus n+4. Strict discrete concavity of baseline M sqrt(j) dominates bounded perturbations, making y_i=A_{n-i+1}-A_{n-i} positive increasing integers and b=(1+y1,y2-y1,...) positive. All T realized, max tangent count n+sum_{j<=floor(sqrt n)} binom(n,j²). Independently programmed all nonempty square-index subsets and nonsquare singletons for n=2..21, checking reconstruction, integer positivity, strict concavity, and minima with 65-digit decimal arithmetic. That is bounded corroboration, not proof of all n; exact irrational-obstruction/concavity prove all n.
